desc: 205 lead from 5010 run 3: SIQ_CFG_EL1 is the only named register that differs between the boot core (0, iBoot) and every secondary (3, reset); 208's reproducer faulted at maxcpus=2 (cpu0+E cpu1), so the asymmetry to test is boot-vs-every-secondary. m1n1 writes SIQ_CFG_EL1=2 on every core for M1-M3 (chickens.c .siq_cfg) but features_m4 omits it. Experiment: patches/m1n1-t6040-siq-cfg.patch (-DT6040_SIQ_CFG adds .siq_cfg=true to features_m4) on m1n1 80badc91; control = same tree/toolchain without the define (ELFs differ in exactly 1 byte). NEW WRITE CLASS: msr to a CPU-core IMP-DEF register (SIQ_CFG_EL1 = 2) that m1n1 already writes on all M1-M3 cores; not PMU/SMC/SPMI/NVRAM/MMIO. Steps: (1) chainload siq m1n1, 5010 script (reads) shows cpu0/cpu1/cpu5 = 2; (2) 208 BusyBox reproducer (scripts/t6040-cow-repro.sh) on the daily+NVMe-free kernel/RAM root at maxcpus=2 x4 and maxcpus=6 x4 with the siq m1n1, and the same with the control m1n1 x4 each, same day, fresh boot per run; (3) variant B (write 0 on secondaries to match iBoot cpu0) only if 2 changes nothing. No storage writes.
author: claude

hashes.build: worktree of m1n1 80badc91, rustup nightly, M1N1_VERSION_TAG=v1.6.0-wallace-80badc91; ELF/bin differ in exactly 1 byte (features_m4.siq_cfg)
hashes.proposal: per (variant, maxcpus in {2,6}): 2 fresh boots x 4 in-boot reproducer runs (initramfs-cow-report); 8 boots + 1 verify
